note: Self-contained oracle case over a multi-module app (ten modules). It installs no third-party package and is not replay-driven: it is proven directly with effect='canary_sql' against the SQLite database run.sql_db declares (a copy of it is seeded with the canary table; the original is never touched). The injectable statement is assembled in shop/repository.py, two calls below the route handler (routes.search_products -> services.search_catalog -> ProductRepository.find), so the graph slice has real hops to cut. No upstream repo/commit applies because the code is original synthetic code written for this case.

real_world_analog.fix: Joomla 3.7.1 escapes list.fullordering and list.direction before they reach the ORDER BY clause. The general fix for the class is an allow-list of sortable columns plus bound parameters for values, which is what the fixed tree does.
real_world_analog.related: CVE-2014-3704 (Drupal 7 expandArguments): the placeholders of an IN list were built from caller-controlled array keys. The IN-list exploit in this case models the same family (a statement assembled from a list).
real_world_analog.summary: SQL injection in the com_fields component of Joomla 3.7.0: the list[fullordering] request parameter reached the model's ORDER BY clause unsanitized, without authentication. The pattern is a sort parameter reaching the ORDER BY of a list query.
real_world_analog.verification: CVE numbers and summaries confirmed via web search (Joomla security centre, NVD, Sucuri, Drupal SA-CORE-2014-005) on 2026-10-31; the app in this case is original synthetic code, not Joomla or Drupal.

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the sort text is only checked to be made of identifier-like characters, so a quote-free boolean expression over the canary table still gets into the ORDER BY; the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
